publication.title: Deigmata: A User-Centered Visualization Tool for Knowledge Graph Exploration
publication.version: Published December 2025 article; not excluded as merely a review because it reports its own artifact and interviews

source_reading.scope: Publication front matter, DSR/model methodology, interviews, Deigmata feature matrix/tool description and conclusion/limitations (§§3–5).

adjudication.basis: The primary report contributes the Deigmata KG visualization prototype alongside a literature-based design model. Its implemented features and repository are reported, but the 14-person evaluation validates the process model through interviews rather than measured user interaction with the deployed prototype.

codes.notes: Deigmata capabilities are source-author feature coding; runtime graph model/stack and operational usability not established. Interviews validate model, not task performance on prototype. Chronology/tree/heatmap features are reported; no inferred node-link implementation or recommendation engine.

descriptions.interaction: KG node expansion/inspection, glossary/tree support, chronological views, graph metrics, heatmap/background aids and collaborative expert/regular-user roles.
descriptions.guidance: Process triggers for expert help and objective revision; visual aids for pattern recognition.
descriptions.visualisation: ["KG expansion and node detail", "Tree/glossary", "Chronological views", "Heatmaps/background clustering aids", "Graph metrics"]
descriptions.evaluation: SLR-informed DSR process and 14 semi-structured interviews on the proposed model; nine-feature comparison of own prototype and eight existing tools.

resources.notes: README names DEIGMATA and cites matching DOI10.31083/KO46137; current tree includes api/web and a compose file. This does not verify the historical paper version or feature completeness.

report_level_evaluation.design: SLR-informed DSR process and 14 semi-structured interviews on the proposed model; nine-feature comparison of own prototype and eight existing tools.
report_level_evaluation.participants: participants: 14; population: Seven postgraduate students and seven computer-science experts with at least five years of experience
report_level_evaluation.results: Not reported; limits: Interview script presents process model step by step and requests comments; no controlled prototype task-time/accuracy/usability test established. Nine tools/features and 497 reviewed studies are not user participants. Prototype is explicitly not production ready.
report_level_evaluation.limitations: Not reported: tasks, comparator, measures, results. Interview script presents process model step by step and requests comments; no controlled prototype task-time/accuracy/usability test established. Nine tools/features and 497 reviewed studies are not user participants. Prototype is explicitly not production ready.
